findings.summary: The bounded-executor regression covers only async waiters and misses the production mixed sync-facade deadlock.
findings.diagnosis: The new condition makes async waiters consume no executor workers, but non-event-loop synchronous callers still block in Condition.wait() while the async owner submits _install_and_startup through the same default executor. The bounded-executor test queues only ensure_initialized_async calls, and the sync-refusal test invokes ensure_initialized directly on the event-loop thread, so neither exercises a synchronous ensure_initialized call already occupying a default-executor worker. The critical starvation contract therefore remains unverified, and the current implementation can deadlock in that caller shape.
findings.evidence: test_bounded_executor_burst_cannot_starve_transaction_owner__b102 at lines 142-185 creates every queued caller with ensure_initialized_async(), while test_sync_initializer_refuses_async_owner_without_blocking__b102 at lines 188-214 calls ensure_initialized() inline on the active event loop and reaches the typed-refusal branch. No changed test runs a public asyncio.to_thread-backed synchronous facade concurrently with an async transaction owner under one- and two-worker executors.
findings.correction: Add deterministic one- and two-worker counterfactuals in which ensure_initialized_async owns the transaction while public to_thread-backed synchronous facade callers occupy the bounded default executor; assert every caller terminates without starvation and that the runtime reaches the intended terminal state. The test must fail against both the prior executor-lock implementation and the current condition implementation until sync acquisition can no longer block owner startup behind those workers.
